name: volmanaged_v0
hypothesis: VOLATILITY-MANAGED EXPOSURE (Moreira and Muir 2017; Harvey et al. 2018; Bollerslev, Hood, Huss and Pedersen 2018). Past realised variance forecasts future variance well, but it forecasts future returns only weakly. A long NQ book that scales exposure by c / (recent realised variance) should therefore earn a positive alpha against the unmanaged buy-and-hold at the same average exposure, and a higher Sharpe ratio. Tested claim for NQ in-sample: a daily-checked, inverse-variance-scaled long MNQ book on $1,000,000 notional capital (cap 2.0x, no-trade band 0.10, real-time scaling constant) has (i) a positive Moreira-Muir spanning alpha against the same-exposure buy-and-hold MNQ book, net of costs, and (ii) a higher Sharpe ratio. This is SIZING, not direction timing: the book is always long, so NQ's 2010-2021 drift cannot pass it. The drift sits in b*r_bh, and the Sharpe comparison is scale-free. PRIOR: moderate for the effect and weak for detecting it here. Published evidence for the US market: Moreira-Muir market alpha 4.86%/yr (SE 1.56), appraisal ratio 0.34, Sharpe 0.52 vs 0.42 over 1926-2015. Harvey et al. S&P 500 futures 1988-2017: Sharpe 0.50 unscaled vs 0.59-0.63 scaled with 5-minute intraday volatility. The critiques are strong. Cederburg et al. 2020: across 103 strategies, the scaled version beats the original in only 53 cases. The market Sharpe gain is 0.09 with Jobson-Korkie p 0.30 over 90 years, and real-time combinations underperform (market 0.42 vs 0.46) because of structural breaks. Liu, Tang and Zhou 2019: the full-sample c is look-ahead, and the corrected strategy outperforms only in the financial crisis. Harvey et al.: the Sharpe gain is confined to risk assets (the leverage effect), and the robust benefit is a thinner left tail. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: Bollerslev et al. 2018 do not document Sharpe gains. Their utility framework assumes a CONSTANT conditional Sharpe ratio (RFS p.2756) and values better risk forecasts at about 0.5% of wealth per year. They are cited here for the method (5-minute RV, HAR-type forecasts, slow trading), not as evidence of alpha. POWER (literature only, computed before results): the evaluation runs about 10.7 years, so a t of 2.0 needs an appraisal ratio of about 0.61. The published market appraisal ratios are 0.32-0.46, which give an expected alpha t of about 1.0-1.5 and P(t >= 2) of about 17-31%. The expected Sharpe gain (0.09-0.13) has an SE of about 0.17-0.26, so z is about 0.35-0.75. A FAIL is the most likely outcome even if NQ behaves like the published US market, and a FAIL would not refute Moreira-Muir.
rule: ONE HEADLINE RULE, frozen before any NQ data is read. DATA: bars = nq_lab.data.serve(pd.Timestamp('2010-01-01', tz='UTC'), pd.Timestamp('2022-01-01', tz='UTC'), caller='volmanaged_screen', reason='<pre-registered volmanaged_v0 in-sample screen>', variant='repaired'). These are 1-minute NQ.V.0 bars, additively back-adjusted, with ts = bar OPEN in UTC. Fill missing raw_c with calendar_report.fill_raw_c, then build calendar_effects.Bars.from_frame. Sessions come from sessions.nyse_sessions(2010-09-28, 2021-12-31). Unrepairable days come from calendar_report.repair_days (2010-09-28 included). Nothing dated 2022 or later is read. PRICES: for session d with open_utc O_d and close_utc X_d, the trade price is P_close(d) = calendar_effects.close_quote(bars, X_d), i.e. c of the bar with ts == X_d - 1 min (15:59 ET, or 12:59 ET on 13:00 early closes). Every order fills at exactly this price. The grid price at time tau is g(tau) = calendar_effects.price_before(bars, tau, 5), i.e. c of the latest bar with tau-5min <= ts < tau. g(O_d) = o of the bar with ts == O_d, and it must exist. SIGNAL CUTOFF (strictly before the close): every input to the decision at the close of d comes from bars with ts <= X_d - 6 min, which is the bar stamped 15:54 ET that ends at 15:55 ET (12:54 ET on early closes), or from earlier sessions. Nothing from 15:55-16:00 ET of day d enters the decision, so there is a 5-minute gap between the last input and the fill. DAILY RTH REALISED VARIANCE (5-minute returns from 1-minute bars, RTH only): grid tau_i = O_d + 5i min for i = 0..n_d, with tau_{n_d} = X_d - 5 min. That gives n_d = 77 intervals from 09:30 to 15:55 on full days and 41 on early closes. Returns are r_{d,i} = (g(tau_i) - g(tau_{i-1})) / raw_c of the bar behind g(tau_{i-1}): back-adjusted point differences over the unadjusted price level, never logs of back-adjusted prices. RV_d = sum_i r_{d,i}^2. No overnight return and no 15:55-16:00 interval enter RV on any day, which keeps repaired (RTH-only) days and vendor days identical in construction. RV_d is VALID iff the 09:30 bar exists, at most 8 of the n_d grid prices are missing (a missing grid price carries the previous one forward), and every |r_{d,i}| <= guards.CONSTANTS['max_abs_1m_move'] (0.10). Otherwise RV_d = NaN and the day is listed. VARIANCE ESTIMATE (Moreira-Muir's 'previous month', rolled daily): sigma2_d = mean of the valid RV over the 22 realised sessions ending with d (d included, since its RV is complete at 15:55). It is defined only if at least 17 of the 22 are valid. SCALING CONSTANT (real time, and it GATES): leverage cap L = 2.0. c_d solves mean_{s in H_d} min(c / sigma2_s, L) = 1.0 by bisection (relative tolerance 1e-10), where H_d = all defined sigma2_s with s < d, an expanding window from the first defined sigma2. c_d is defined only when |H_d| >= 126. The expanding window keeps the capped rule's average exposure on PAST data equal to 1.0x without using the future. TARGET: w*_d = min(c_d / sigma2_d, L), a fraction of K = $1,000,000 notional. The book is long-only (w* > 0). CONTRACTS: K is fixed and not compounded. N*_d = round(w*_d * K / (2 * p_d)) MNQ, where p_d = raw_c of the latest bar with ts in [X_d - 10 min, X_d - 5 min), i.e. the 15:54 bar or up to 4 minutes earlier. Held exposure before trading: w_hat_d = N_prev * 2 * p_d / K. REBALANCING (checked daily, with a no-trade band): at each close d where c_d, sigma2_d, p_d and P_close(d) all exist, N_d = N*_d if |w*_d - w_hat_d| > B = 0.10, or the book is rolling at d, or d is the first trading session T0. Otherwise N_d = N_prev. When any of those inputs is missing, N_d = N_prev (no trade). The book is rolling at d when the instrument_id of the 15:54 bar differs from the instrument_id of P_close(prev). Charging uses roll_d = iid(P_close(d)) != iid(P_close(prev)), and any disagreement between the two roll flags is listed. T0 = the first session where c_d is defined (expected around May 2011, UNVERIFIED). COSTS per contract per side: 0 tick = $0.61, 1 tick = 0.25 pt * $2 + $0.61 = $1.11 (base), 2 ticks = $1.61 (stress). cost_d = |N_d - N_prev| * s on non-roll days and (N_prev + N_d) * s on roll days: close everything in the old contract and reopen N_d in the new one. The entry at T0 and the liquidation at the last close (2021-12-31) are charged to both books. P&L: P&L_d = N_prev * $2 * (P_close(d) - P_close(prev)) - cost_d, where prev is the latest earlier session with a close quote. Spanning days are flagged as in calendar_seasonal.daily_changes. r_d = P&L_d / K. Futures returns are already excess returns, and interest on K is ignored for both books. Evaluation sessions are every session after T0 with a close quote, through 2021-12-31. SAME-EXPOSURE BUY-AND-HOLD CONTROL: k = mean over the evaluation sessions of the managed book's held exposure N_prev * 2 * raw_c(P_close(prev)) / K. This is ex post and used only for the benchmark; the alpha t and both Sharpe ratios are invariant to k. The BH book holds N_BH = round(k * K / (2 * raw_c)), set at the T0 close and reset only at roll closes, with the identical cost and P&L rules, giving r_bh,d. HEADLINE STATISTICS: (a) annualised Sharpe = mean(r) / sd(r, ddof=1) * sqrt(252) for both books at 0, 1 and 2 ticks. (b) The Moreira-Muir spanning regression r_m,d = a + b * r_bh,d + e_d, with both books at the same cost level, using calendar_stats.ols_hac with lags 5 and 21. The gating t_a = min(t at 5 lags, t at 21 lags). Annual alpha = 252 * a, in % of K. (c) The same regression run separately within each of calendar_report.BLOCKS (2010-13 = T0..2013-12-31, 2014-17, 2018-21), assigning days by P&L date. (d) dSR = SR_managed - SR_bh. Implementation: a pandas screen script that refuses a bare invocation, like calendar_screen.py. The spec is frozen as experiments/volmanaged_v0.json with its sha256, and results go to results/screens/volmanaged_v0.json. A result is cited only after a Nautilus reproduction through backtests/run_base.py (a registry strategy with a multiplier-2 synthetic MNQ on NQ bars) matches contracts, P&L and Sharpe exactly and passes the balance check, then goes into the ledger via scripts/ledger_append.py.
comparisons: SAME-EXPOSURE BUY-AND-HOLD (gating): the regression alpha and the Sharpe difference against the BH book at k = the managed book's realised mean exposure, at 0, 1 and 2 ticks. Also reported: BH at k = 1.0, and the regression on the frictionless index return dc / raw_c(prev), as a check that the alpha does not come from BH rounding or roll resets.

SHARPE-DIFFERENCE TEST (reported with the verdict, not gating): Ledoit-Wolf (2008) studentised circular block bootstrap of dSR at 1 and 2 ticks, block b = 10 sessions (inside LW's candidate grid {1,2,4,6,8,10}), 4,999 replications, seed 20260926, one-sided p for H1: SR_managed > SR_bh, plus the 90% interval. Also reported: the Memmel (2003) corrected Jobson-Korkie z, i.e. dSR / sqrt(theta / T) with theta = 2 - 2 rho + 0.5 (SR_m^2 + SR_bh^2 - 2 SR_m SR_bh rho^2) on per-session Sharpe ratios, and the project's existing percentile moving-block bootstrap (overnight_drift.sharpe_gap_bootstrap).

LOOK-AHEAD c (Moreira-Muir exact, secondary): a constant c solved on the whole evaluation window, same cap. Moreira-Muir footnote 5 says c does not change the Sharpe ratio, so any gap between this and the headline shows how much comes from the cap and rounding interacting with c (the Liu-Tang-Zhou point).

MONTHLY REBALANCING (Moreira-Muir primary frequency): trade only at the last session of each calendar month to min(c_d / sigma2_month, L), where sigma2_month = mean RV of that month's sessions (through 15:55 on the last day), with the same real-time c logic.
DAILY WITHOUT A BAND (B = 0), and Bollerslev et al.'s 'gradual' rule: trade 15% of the gap to target each day.
INVERSE VOLATILITY instead of variance: w* = min(c' / sqrt(sigma2_d), L), with c' solved the same way (Harvey et al.; Moreira-Muir Table 5 reports the same Sharpe with lower turnover).

HAR-RV FORECAST (Corsi 2009; Bollerslev et al. 2018): forecast of the mean RV over the next 22 sessions = b0 + bd RV_d + bw mean(RV_{d-4..d}) + bm mean(RV_{d-21..d}), fitted by OLS on an expanding window using only targets fully observed before d (minimum 252 pairs), floored at the minimum past RV. w* = min(c'' / forecast, L).
EXTRA ONE-DAY LAG (Harvey et al. use returns up to t-2): sigma2 ends at d-1, to show sensitivity to the 5-minute signal-to-fill gap.
LEVERAGE CAPS 1.0, 1.5, 3.0 and uncapped (Moreira-Muir Table 5: alpha 2.12 at a cap of 1 and 3.10 at 1.5), each with its own real-time c.
NQ-LOT VERSION: integer NQ contracts ($20/pt, $2.24 per side). This checks that the result is not an artefact of MNQ's higher fee per notional.
SUBSAMPLED RV: the average of 5 grids offset 0-4 minutes (Bollerslev et al. 2018 p.2735) instead of the single 09:30-anchored grid.

EXPOSURE-SHIFT PLACEBO: circularly shift the managed exposure series w* by random offsets of at least 252 sessions (2,000 draws, seed 20260926), re-price at 1 tick, and give the percentile of the actual alpha. This keeps the exposure distribution and persistence but breaks the alignment with volatility.
VOLATILITY-QUINTILE DIAGNOSTIC (Moreira-Muir Figure 1; Harvey et al. Exhibit 4): next-session NQ % return, sd, and mean/variance by quintile of sigma2_d.

TAILS (Harvey et al.'s claimed main benefit): vol of vol (sd of the rolling 252-session sd of 21-session overlapping returns), 1% and 5% mean shortfall of 21-session overlapping returns, maximum drawdown and skewness, for the managed and BH books.

COST LADDER AND TURNOVER: alpha and dSR at 0, 1 and 2 ticks. Break-even ticks per side at which alpha = 0 (Moreira-Muir Table 4: 56 bp for monthly variance scaling). Harvey turnover = 252 * mean |daily exposure change| / (2 * mean exposure). Number of rebalancing days and roll count.
STABILITY: leave-one-year-out alpha t, per-year alpha, and the per-block b (the Cederburg et al. structural-instability concern).
pass_bar: PASS only if ALL of (1)-(3) hold for the headline rule (MNQ, K = $1,000,000, L = 2.0, B = 0.10, real-time expanding c, rolls charged). (1) ALPHA: t_a = min(HAC-5 t, HAC-21 t) of the intercept in r_m = a + b r_bh >= 2.0, with BOTH books net of 1-tick costs ($1.11 per MNQ per side). (2) BLOCKS: the per-block regression intercept a > 0 in each of 2010-13 (T0..2013-12-31), 2014-17 and 2018-21, at 1 tick. (3) SHARPE: SR_managed - SR_bh > 0 with BOTH books net of 2-tick costs ($1.61 per side). All three require beating the same-exposure buy-and-hold, so NQ's drift alone cannot pass. VALIDITY is not a performance test: if any of these fails, the run is INVALID and gets no verdict until the fault is fixed. (a) The no-look-ahead guards pass and were shown to fail first on a deliberately leaky version (born failing): perturbing any bar with ts >= 15:55 ET on day d, or any data of later sessions, must leave N_d unchanged, and c_d must not change when sigma2_s for s >= d is altered. (b) Held exposure never exceeds L by more than one contract. (c) At least 2,400 evaluation sessions and at least 95% valid RV days. (d) The daily P&L sum equals total book P&L to the cent. REPORTED WITH THE VERDICT, NOT GATING: the Ledoit-Wolf studentised block-bootstrap one-sided p and the Memmel z for dSR > 0 at 1 tick. Bonferroni over the 9 NQ hypotheses tested (za ORB, intraday momentum, turn-of-month, pre-holiday, pre-FOMC, overnight, macro-day, Halloween, this one): print p_one_sided(t_a) x 9. The one-sided 0.05/9 threshold is t of about 2.54. If 2.0 <= t_a < 2.54, the verdict line reads 'PASS (not significant after Bonferroni, family 9)'. That label cannot turn a FAIL into a PASS or the reverse. POWER WARNING (from the literature only, fixed before results): the evaluation window runs from about May 2011 to 2021-12-31, T of about 10.7 years (UNVERIFIED until built). The expected alpha t is roughly AR x sqrt(T). Published US-market appraisal ratios are 0.32 (Cederburg et al. 1926-2016; Harvey et al. daily, t 3.05 over 91 years), 0.34 (Moreira-Muir 1926-2015), 0.46 (Moreira-Muir 1986-2015 subsample, alpha 4.22 with SE 1.66 over 30 years), and about 0.37 implied for S&P futures (Sharpe 0.62 vs 0.50 with daily rho of about 0.85). That gives E[t] of about 1.05-1.50 and P(t_a >= 2) of about 17-31%. Each 3.5-year block alone has E[t] of about 0.6-0.9. The Sharpe gain has SE of about sqrt(2(1 - rho) / T) = 0.17 (rho 0.85) to 0.26 (rho 0.63). Against a published gain of 0.09-0.13, z is about 0.35-0.75, P(dSR > 0) is about 0.63-0.78, and a one-sided 5% LW test has power of only about 10-19%. The joint probability of passing (1)-(3), if NQ carries the published US effect, is roughly 12-25%. Under a zero effect it is about 1-2%. A FAIL is expected and is not evidence against Moreira-Muir; a PASS would be informative.
pitfalls: LOOK-AHEAD IN c (Liu, Tang and Zhou 2019): Moreira-Muir choose c on the full sample. With a constant c the Sharpe ratio and alpha t are unchanged, but once a leverage cap, integer contracts or costs apply, a full-sample c leaks the future. The headline uses the expanding real-time c_d, and the full-sample c is secondary only.

SPANNING ALPHA IS NOT AN IMPLEMENTABLE IMPROVEMENT (Cederburg et al. 2020): alpha > 0 with b < 1 can coexist with a LOWER Sharpe ratio than buy-and-hold (Cederburg: 77 of 103 alphas positive, yet only 53 Sharpe gains). That is why criterion (3) is part of PASS. Never quote the alpha without dSR.

STRUCTURAL INSTABILITY: Cederburg et al. find about 2.4 Bai-Perron breaks per spanning regression on average. Three blocks over about 10.7 years cannot rule this out, so report per-block b and a, and leave-one-year-out.

THE BH SCALE k IS EX POST: that is harmless for the gating statistics (the alpha t and both Sharpe ratios are scale-invariant, and costs scale with contracts), but the dollar P&L comparison with BH uses ex-post information. Say so wherever dollars are quoted.

RTH-ONLY VARIANCE: repaired 2010-2015 days hold only 09:30-16:00 bars, so the overnight return and the 15:55-16:00 interval are excluded on EVERY day for consistency. Bollerslev et al. add overnight squared returns. RTH RV understates close-to-close variance, but the level is absorbed by c. Days whose risk is mostly overnight (gaps) are under-weighted. Never mix in pre-open bars on vendor days only.

BACK-ADJUSTED LEVELS: 5-minute returns divide back-adjusted POINT differences by the raw price (raw_c). Logs or ratios of back-adjusted prices are wrong under additive adjustment. Contract counts use raw_c, and P&L uses back-adjusted c differences.

SIGNAL-TO-FILL GAP: the last input is the 15:54 bar (ends 15:55 ET) and the fill is the 15:59 bar's c (the last trade before 16:00, not the CME settlement). The 1-tick slippage is assumed, not measured, for a close-time MNQ order. The extra-lag secondary checks sensitivity.

MNQ DID NOT TRADE BEFORE MAY 2019 (UNVERIFIED launch date): the pre-2019 book is hypothetical MNQ priced off NQ bars at MNQ fees. MNQ's $0.61 per side is costlier per notional than NQ's $2.24 per 10 MNQ-equivalents, so the NQ-lot secondary is required.

LEVERAGE CAP x c INTERACTION: c_d is solved on the capped rule, so the cap binding more or less often changes the average exposure and the alpha level. The cap (2.0) and band (0.10) are fixed now and must not be tuned. Cap and band variants are secondary only.

CRASH AFTER CALM: the inverse-variance rule is most levered right after quiet periods. A gap-down after low volatility (the jump-risk channel Moreira-Muir discuss) hits hardest at up to 2x. Report the worst days and their exposure.

MISSING CLOSES AND GATED DAYS: 6 unrepairable 2014 days, 4 March-2020 limit-down days and 2010-09-28. On a session without a close quote there is no trade, and P&L spans to the next close (flagged). Missing RV days drop out of the 22-session mean (at least 17 valid required). The COVID days fall exactly when de-risking matters, so list what the book held on them.

ROLLS: the NQ.V.0 volume roll can flip A->B->A. The book charges each close-to-close instrument change as a full close and reopen, and reports flip counts. Roll gaps in the stitched series differ by 0.25-2 points from other products (nq-lab project rules). This is negligible for daily P&L but should be listed.

AUTOCORRELATED, HETEROSKEDASTIC DAILY RETURNS: gate on min(HAC-5, HAC-21). The i.i.d. Memmel z is reported only alongside the LW studentised bootstrap, which allows for serial dependence and heavy tails.

LITERATURE MISMATCH: the evidence is on the CRSP value-weighted market and S&P 500 futures, mostly over 30-90-year samples. The Nasdaq-100 is more volatile and concentrated. Moreira-Muir alphas were weaker in 1956-1985, when volatility varied less, so a period with fewer volatility regimes lowers the expected alpha.

BRIEF'S CLAIM ABOUT BOLLERSLEV ET AL. IS WRONG: their framework assumes a constant Sharpe ratio and reports utility gains from better risk forecasts, not Sharpe gains. Do not cite them as evidence that the Sharpe ratio rises.

NON-COMPOUNDING RETURNS: returns are P&L on a fixed $1M, so Sharpe and alpha are on additive daily P&L. Compounding changes nothing material for Sharpe but changes drawdown figures, so state the convention.

SINGLE PRE-REGISTERED FORM: only the headline (inverse variance, 22-session RTH RV, daily check, band 0.10, cap 2.0, real-time c) gates. If a secondary passes where the headline fails, that is a new hypothesis for a new pre-registration, not a result.
evidence: Moreira and Muir (2017), 'Volatility-Managed Portfolios', Journal of Finance 72(4):1611-1644, doi 10.1111/jofi.12513: https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1111/jofi.12513 (abstract: managed portfolios that take less risk when volatility is high produce large alphas and higher Sharpe ratios for the market and other factors).

Moreira-Muir working paper, NBER w22208: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w22208/w22208.pdf. Eq. (1)-(2), pp.5-6: f_sigma = c / sigma_hat^2 * f, with sigma_hat^2 = realised variance of the previous month's 22 daily returns. c is chosen so the managed portfolio has the same unconditional sd, and footnote 5 says 'c has no effect on our strategy's Sharpe ratio, thus the fact that we use the full sample to compute c does not impact our results'. p.7 and Table 1: market alpha 4.86%/yr (SE 1.56), beta 0.61, R^2 0.37, rmse 51.39, N 1,065 months. p.8: appraisal ratio 0.34. Table 2: original market Sharpe 0.42; subsample alphas 1926-55 8.11 (3.09), 1956-85 2.06 (2.82), 1986-2015 4.22 (1.66).

Moreira-Muir NBER w22208, Table 4 (p.33): monthly variance scaling has mean |dw| 0.73, alpha 4.86% falling to 4.77/3.98/3.63% at 1/10/14 bp costs, break-even 56 bp. Inverse vol: |dw| 0.38, break-even 84 bp. Caps at 1 and 1.5: |dw| 0.16, break-even 110 and 161 bp. Table 5 (p.34): weight percentiles P50 0.93, P75 1.59, P90 2.64, P99 6.39. Managed Sharpe 0.52. Inverse-vol Sharpe 0.53 with P99 3.36. No leverage: alpha 2.12 (0.71). 50% leverage: alpha 3.10 (0.98), Sharpe 0.53. Figure 6: alphas decline as the rebalancing horizon lengthens. Appendix A.2: across 20 OECD indices the managed Sharpe is 0.15 higher on average and higher in 80% of cases.

Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020), 'On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios', JFE 138(1):95-117, doi 10.1016/j.jfineco.2020.04.015. Abstract: https://www.ssrn.com/abstract=3357038 (via search). Full text: https://www.lehigh.edu/~xuy219/research/COWY.pdf. Table 1: MKT Sharpe 0.42 original vs 0.51 managed, difference 0.09, Jobson-Korkie p 0.30 (1926-2016), P99 of the managed MKT weight 6.47, correlation with the original 0.63. Table 2: 53 of 103 Sharpe differences positive (8 significant). Table 3: MKT spanning alpha 4.63% (t 3.08), appraisal ratio 0.32. Table 5: real-time combination for MKT, Sharpe 0.42 vs 0.46 for the original, using a 120-month expanding window and |y| <= 5. Table 9: on average 2.37 Bai-Perron breaks per spanning regression. Footnote 8: the Jobson-Korkie test with the Memmel (2003) correction.

Liu, Tang and Zhou (2019), 'Volatility-Managed Portfolio: Does It Really Work?', Journal of Portfolio Management 46(1):38-51, doi 10.3905/jpm.2019.1.107: https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.3905/jpm.2019.1.107. A typical market application suffers look-ahead bias. After correction, maximum drawdowns are 68%-93%, and the strategy outperforms only during the financial crisis. Also https://profiles.wustl.edu/en/publications/volatility-managed-portfolio-does-it-really-work/

Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison and Van Hemert (2018), 'The Impact of Volatility Targeting', JPM 45(1):14-33, doi 10.3905/jpm.2018.45.1.014: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P135_The_impact_of.pdf. p.16: scaled return = r_t * sigma_target / sigma_{t-2}, using returns up to t-2, with EWMA volatility; 5-minute RV over 9:15-14:00 CT for S&P futures. p.17: costs of 1 bp of notional for equities, and turnover defined as mean |daily exposure change| x 252 / (2 x mean exposure). Exhibit 5 (US equities 1927-2017): Sharpe 0.40 unscaled vs 0.48-0.51 scaled; 1% mean shortfall -11.4% vs -8.3 to -10.1%; vol of vol 4.6% vs 1.7-2.2%. Footnote 14: intercept t 3.05 (Newey-West, 30 lags), R^2 0.73. Exhibit 8 (S&P 500 futures 1988-2017): Sharpe 0.50 unscaled, 0.56-0.60 with daily data, 0.59-0.63 with 5-minute intraday data, with net approximately equal to gross. Abstract (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.3905/jpm.2018.45.1.014): the gain is limited to risk assets (the leverage effect), negligible for bonds, FX and commodities, and left-tail events are less severe.

Bollerslev, Hood, Huss and Pedersen (2018), 'Risk Everywhere: Modeling and Managing Volatility', RFS 31(7):2729-2773, doi 10.1093/rfs/hhy041: https://public.econ.duke.edu/~boller/Published_Papers/rfs_18.pdf. p.2734-2735: 5-minute RV, averaged over five subsampled grids starting at the first five 1-minute marks, with overnight squared returns added. p.2756: the utility framework assumes a constant conditional Sharpe ratio. Table 6 (p.2759), equities realised utility with zero costs: static 2.93%, 21-day RV 3.53%, HAR 3.55%, HExp 3.62%. p.2763: costs set at the full bid-ask spread, and 'gradual' trading 15% of the way to target per day restores part of the utility lost to costs. p.2764: the models are worth close to 0.5% of wealth per year relative to a static model.

Corsi (2009), 'A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility', Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2):174-196, doi 10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001: https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001 (HAR-RV with daily, weekly and monthly components).

Ledoit and Wolf (2008), 'Robust performance hypothesis testing with the Sharpe ratio', Journal of Empirical Finance 15(5):850-859, doi 10.1016/j.jempfin.2008.03.002: https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/j.jempfin.2008.03.002. Method as summarised by search: a studentised time-series (circular block) bootstrap for the Sharpe difference that is robust to serial dependence and heavy tails, HAC via a prewhitened QS kernel, and a data-dependent block size chosen from {1,2,4,6,8,10}. builder_resolutions: V1 T0: the first session with a close quote at which c_d is defined AND sigma2_d and p_d exist, so the entry trade can happen. The literal 'first session where c_d is defined' is printed next to it; if the two differ the gap is listed.

V2 Evaluation sessions are the sessions after T0 with a close quote through the last session <= 2021-12-31 with one. The T0 entry cost (paid at the T0 close, before the first evaluation session) is booked on the first evaluation session, so the daily series sums to the whole-book P&L. At the last evaluation session N = 0 (liquidation) overrides the rebalance rule, for both books.
V3 round() is round-half-away-from-zero (floor(x + 0.5) for x >= 0), not Python's banker's rounding, for every contract count.

V4 RV grid: every grid lookup is restricted to bars with ts >= O_d, so no pre-open bar can enter (for the headline grid, tau >= O_d + 5 min, this changes nothing). The 'at most 8 of the n_d grid prices missing' count runs over i = 1..n_d; g(tau_0) is the separate 09:30-bar requirement. A carried-forward grid price carries its bar's raw_c too. The denominator of r_1 is raw_c of the 09:30 bar. A NaN return (raw_c missing after fill_raw_c) makes RV_d invalid.

V5 Validity (b): between trades the held exposure can legitimately drift above L inside the no-trade band (no trade while w_hat <= w* + B), so the literal check at every close would fail by design, not by fault. Gate (b) is: after every trade N_d * 2 * p_d / K <= L + 2 * p_d / K (one contract), and after every decision with inputs present N_d * 2 * p_d / K <= L + B + 2 * p_d / K. The maximum held exposure at close prices is reported.
V6 Validity (c): the valid-RV share is over all 2,836 realised sessions 2010-09-28..2021-12-31 (a session without bars counts as invalid).

V7 Validity (a) at run time: on 12 evaluation days sampled with seed 20260926, every bar with ts >= X_d - 5 min (day d and all later data) is scaled by random factors and the decision chain is recomputed; the N path through d, and c_d, must be unchanged. Unit tests show the same guard failing on deliberately leaky decision functions and a leaky c solver (born failing).

V8 The forced-rebalance roll flag uses the iid of the sizing bar (latest bar in [X_d - 10 min, X_d - 5 min)) against iid(P_close(prev)); costs use roll_d = iid(P_close(d)) != iid(P_close(prev)) and are (|N_prev| + |N_d|) * s on roll days. A->B->A flips are counted on the sequence of close-quote iids.

V9 Ledoit-Wolf 2008 (paper not read; built from the summaries): delta-method studentisation on v = (mu1, mu2, E r1^2, E r2^2); original-sample Psi from a VAR(1)-prewhitened QS-kernel HAC with the Andrews (1991) AR(1) plug-in bandwidth; bootstrap Psi from the block-sum estimator of the circular block bootstrap; one-sided p = (1 + #{(d* - d) / se* >= d / se}) / (B + 1); 90% interval = [d - q95 * se, d - q05 * se]. Reported, never gating.
V10 Memmel z uses per-session Sharpe ratios (mean / sd with ddof 1), rho = Pearson correlation, z = (SR_m - SR_bh) / sqrt(theta / T); one-sided p from the normal.
V11 Break-even ticks: both books pay the same continuous tick level; bisection on ticks in [0, 400] for a(ticks) = 0; 'none' when a(0) <= 0; '> 400' when a(400) > 0.
V12 Harvey turnover = 252 * mean over evaluation sessions of |N_d - N_prev| * 2 * raw_c(P_close d) / K (roll close/reopen legs excluded), divided by 2 * k.

V13 Monthly variant: decision at the last session of each month that has a close quote (nearest earlier session with one if the last session has none). sigma2_month = mean valid RV of that month's sessions through the decision day, defined with >= 15 valid days. c is solved on the defined sigma2_month of earlier months (expanding), defined with >= 6 earlier months (about 126 sessions). Its own T0 is the first decision at or after the headline T0 with inputs present; no trades between decisions (roll days are still charged as close and reopen at the same N); its own same-exposure BH and evaluation window.

V14 Gradual rule: full entry at T0, then N_d = N_prev + round(0.15 * (N*_d - N_prev)) on every day with inputs present; no forced re-size on roll days (the roll is still charged). B = 0 variant: trade whenever N*_d != N_prev.

V15 HAR: pairs (x_s, y_s) with x_s = (1, RV_s, mean valid RV over s-4..s with >= 3 valid, sigma2_s) and y_s = mean valid RV over sessions s+1..s+22 with >= 17 valid; RV_s must be valid. A pair is usable at d when s + 22 <= idx(d) - 1 (its target is complete before d's session). OLS is refit every session once >= 252 pairs are usable; the forecast at d is x_d beta floored at the minimum valid RV over sessions before d. c'' is solved on past defined forecasts (>= 126), same cap.
V16 Extra-lag variant: sigma2'_d = sigma2 of the previous realised session; c from the sigma2' history with the same rules.
V17 Look-ahead c: one constant c solved on sigma2_d over T0 and all evaluation sessions, same cap 2.0, same T0 and rules.

V18 Caps: 1.0, 1.5, 3.0 and uncapped, each with its own real-time c. With L = 1.0 the equation mean min(c / sigma2, 1) = 1 holds for every c >= max past sigma2; bisection returns the smallest root, so the capped-at-1 book is almost always fully invested (reported as degenerate). Uncapped c = 1 / mean(1 / sigma2) in closed form.
V19 NQ-lot variant: $20/pt, fee $2.24/side, so 0/1/2 ticks = $2.24/$7.24/$12.24 per contract per side; same K, cap, band and T0; own same-exposure BH in NQ lots.

V20 Subsampled RV: grids offset j = 0..4 min; grid j starts at g(O_d + j) (for j > 0 the c of the latest bar in [O_d, O_d + j)) and ends at the last point <= X_d - 5 min; the day is valid only if all five grids pass the headline validity rule; RV = mean of the five.

V21 Exposure-shift placebo: offsets are uniform integers in [252, n - 252] on the index of T0 plus the evaluation sessions; the shifted w* (its NaN pattern moves with it) drives the same band, roll, T0 and liquidation rules; alpha is taken against the headline BH at 1 tick; percentile = share of placebo alphas strictly below the actual alpha.

V22 Volatility-quintile diagnostic on T0 and the evaluation sessions: next-session % return = (P_close(next) - P_close(d)) / raw_c(P_close d) * 100, next = next session with a close; quintiles of sigma2_d are ex post (descriptive).

V23 Tails: 21-session overlapping sums of daily r; vol of vol = sd (ddof 1) of the rolling 252-window sd (ddof 1) of those sums, times sqrt(12) to annualise; mean shortfall = mean of the worst ceil(1% n) and ceil(5% n) sums; maximum drawdown on cumulative non-compounded P&L in % of K; skewness = scipy.stats.skew(bias=False).

V24 Bonferroni: the spec names a family of 9, but this round freezes two sizing specs, so 10 NQ hypotheses have now been tested (za_v0, the C3 Gao intraday momentum check, 6 calendar specs, volmanaged_v0, tsmom_v0). The screen prints p x 9 (as registered) and p x 10; the verdict label uses the registered 9 with the exact calendar_stats.bonferroni_t(0.05, 9, n). p_one_sided(t_a) is calendar_stats.p_one_sided (Student t, n - 1 df).
V25 The frictionless-index regression uses x_d = (P_close(d) - P_close(prev)) / raw_c(P_close prev).
V26 Leave-one-year-out drops one calendar year of evaluation sessions and re-runs the headline regression (t = min of HAC 5 and 21); per-year alpha is the regression within each year.

V27 BH sizing price: N_BH = round(k * K / (2 * raw_c)) uses raw_c of the close quote at T0 and at each roll close; BH at k = 1.0 is built the same way. The managed monthly and every other variant get their own BH at their own realised mean exposure.

V28 Validity (d): the whole-book P&L is recomputed independently from trade cash flows (sum over trade days of (N_prev - N_d) * $2 * P_close(d), final position 0) minus total costs, and must equal the sum of daily P&L within $0.005.

V29 close_quote may return a non-exact close (a bar in [X_d - 5 min, X_d - 1 min) when the 15:59 bar is missing); it is used as the reused machinery defines it and the count is reported. Such a bar is after the 15:55 cutoff, so it never feeds a decision.
